title: What If You Stepped Off the Space Station?

scenes.text: What if you stepped off the International Space Station? You wouldn't fall. Not for weeks.
The station isn't floating. It's falling around Earth at about seventeen thousand miles an hour, and so would you.
You'd circle the planet every ninety minutes, sixteen laps a day, drifting slowly beside the station you just left.
Thin air still tugs at you, even up there. Your orbit would shrink over weeks to months.
Lower and lower, until at about seventy-eight kilometres the air thickens and you'd streak through it like a meteor.
Falling was never the problem. Missing the ground is the whole trick, and the station never stops doing it.

description:
What if you stepped off the International Space Station?
You wouldn't drop. You'd keep orbiting at about 17,000 mph, circling Earth every 90 minutes, until thin air slowly pulled you down over weeks to months.
What should we run through next?
